# Introduction

The code-review report R001 (10 September 2026) established that the repository’s central claim reproduces and listed seven defects. This report is the figure companion for a presentation. It adds three things R001 did not have: proper concept figures for the method (Part A), a broad batch of *fresh* simulations run in parallel (522 optimisation sweeps over 8 seeds and 9 variation axes, plus two other dynamical systems) that support or qualify the theory’s claims (Parts B–F, H), and the quantification *and fix* of the defects, with before/after figures (Part G). Nothing is re-used from R001: every quantity that overlaps (the headline sweep, the F1/F2 numbers) is recomputed here from a frozen snapshot of the sources, and the bug figures execute the pre-fix and post-fix code side by side.

Two things the reader should keep in mind. First, the optimiser seed matters enormously and is reported everywhere: one of the eight random starts lands on the blow-up plateau at the very first window size and never moves under the repository’s flat penalty (§<a href="#sec:gp" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:gp">7</a>); it is kept in every statistic rather than dropped. Second, the sweep in the committed driver (`fhn_model_selection_mod 8.jl`) had guess propagation *disabled* and used two different monomial orderings for the sweep and the polish (§<a href="#sec:bugs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:bugs">10</a>); the driver is fixed in the same commit as this report.

# Definitions (read before the figures)

Everything used in a caption is defined here, including terms inherited from the manuscript and from R001.

## Model, library and data

The target is FitzHugh–Nagumo,
``` math
\begin{equation}
\dot v = v - \tfrac{1}{3}v^3 - w + 0.5,\qquad \dot w = \tfrac{1}{12.5}\,(v + 0.7 - 0.8\,w),
\end{equation}
```
written as a general two-dimensional cubic polynomial system so that model *selection* (which monomials are present) is part of the task:
``` math
\begin{equation}
\dot x_i = \sum_{j=1}^{J} p_{ij}\,\Theta_j(\mathbf x),\quad i=1,2,\qquad
\Theta = \{1,\ w,\ w^2,\ w^3,\ v,\ vw,\ vw^2,\ v^2,\ v^2 w,\ v^3\},\quad J=10 .
\end{equation}
```
**Read this:** the library order above is the *multi-index* order produced by `helper_functions.jl` and used by `odefun_poly!` (mod 8). The older hard-coded RHS `odefun` (mods 2–7) uses the order $`1,v,w,v^2,vw,w^2,v^3,v^2w,vw^2,w^3`$. The two orders are different permutations of the same 10 monomials; mixing them is finding N1 in §<a href="#sec:bugs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:bugs">10</a>. All coefficient plots here use the library order, with the $`\dot v`$ block (10 entries) followed by the $`\dot w`$ block. The parameter vector $`p\in\mathbb R^{20}`$ has 6 non-zero entries: $`\dot v`$: $`(1)\!=\!0.5`$, $`(w)\!=\!-1`$, $`(v)\!=\!1`$, $`(v^3)\!=\!-1/3`$; $`\dot w`$: $`(1)\!=\!0.056`$, $`(w)\!=\!-0.064`$, $`(v)\!=\!0.08`$ (seven including the $`\dot w`$ constant). The optimisation vector is $`z=[x_0;\,p]\in\mathbb R^{22}`$: the first two entries are a free initial condition that enters only through the term $`\lVert x_0-y_0\rVert^2`$.

Data follow the repository recipe exactly (frozen mod 8 lines 103–157, reproduced to $`6\times10^{-15}`$, gate G3): integrate with the in-house fixed-step Tsit5 at $`\delta t_{\rm fine}=0.01`$ from $`(1,1)`$ to $`T=156`$, keep every 100th point, crop to $`t\in[50,150]`$ and shift to $`t\in[0,100]`$ ($`N=101`$ samples, spacing $`\Delta t=1`$), and add Gaussian noise to each component with standard deviation $`0.05\times`$ that component’s own standard deviation (seed 1287436679). The resulting maximum noise norm is $`\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}=0.159`$ and the noise floor of the data term is $`\tfrac1N\sum_i\lVert\eta_i\rVert^2=0.0052`$.

## Cost function

For a window size $`\kappa`$ (number of data intervals per window, $`1\le\kappa\le N-1`$) the record is cut into $`K=\lceil (N-1)/\kappa\rceil`$ windows; each window is integrated *from the noisy datum at its left node* with $`S`$ fixed Tsit5 sub-steps of length $`\delta t=\Delta t/S`$ per data interval, and
``` math
\begin{equation}
J_\kappa(z)=\frac{1}{N}\Big[\lVert x_0-y_0\rVert^2+\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\big\lVert \hat x(t_{i+1};\,p,\,y_{\tau(i)})-y_{i+1}\big\rVert^2\Big]+\frac{\gamma}{20}\sum_{j=1}^{20}\operatorname{smooth}\ell_1(p_j),
\label{eq:J}
\end{equation}
```
where $`\tau(i)`$ is the last node at or before $`t_i`$, and $`\operatorname{smooth}\ell_1(x)=\alpha^{-1}[\log(1+e^{-\alpha x})+\log(1+e^{\alpha x})]`$ with $`\alpha=500`$ (equal to $`|x|`$ for $`|\alpha x|>40`$). $`\kappa=1`$ is one window per data interval; $`\kappa=N-1=100`$ is single shooting. **Read this:** node states are *not* optimisation variables and no continuity constraint is imposed (unlike textbook multiple shooting); this is the manuscript’s formulation and the repository’s code. If any state exceeds $`10^3`$ in magnitude or becomes NaN during integration, the loss returns the constant $`10^3`$ (*flat blow-up penalty*, a plateau with zero gradient). The *graded* penalty (a variant introduced here) returns $`10^3\,(1+\tfrac{N-1-i}{N-1})+J_{\rm partial}/N`$ when the blow-up occurs at data index $`i`$, so that later blow-ups cost less and a derivative-free optimiser has a direction. The manuscript’s $`J_K`$ (no normalisation, no sparsity term) differs from (<a href="#eq:J" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:J">[eq:J]</a>) by the factor $`1/N`$ and the $`\gamma`$ term; the theory figures (Part B) use $`\gamma=0`$.

## Arms

<div class="description">

Sweep $`\kappa`$ upward through a schedule; the minimiser of each stage is the start of the next. Schedules: FULL $`=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,15,20,25,33,50,75,\allowbreak 100\}`$ (default); SHORT $`=\{1,2,5,10,25,50,100\}`$ for the variation experiments; DENSE $`=\{1,\dots,30,35,40,\dots,100\}`$ (44 stages); COARSE $`=\{1,5,25,100\}`$; JUMP $`=\{1,100\}`$.

As GP but the start of the next stage is the best (lowest-cost) minimiser seen so far.

Every stage starts from the same random seed vector. This is the arm the committed mod 8 driver was running.

Nelder–Mead (Optim.jl, 2500 iterations, default tolerances) unless stated; BFGS and L-BFGS use the exact ForwardDiff gradient of (<a href="#eq:J" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:J">[eq:J]</a>) through the integrator (possible only after fix F4), same iteration cap, $`g_{\rm tol}=10^{-8}`$.

Optimiser seed $`s\in\{1,\dots,8\}`$: $`z_{\rm seed}=[y_0;\ 0.1\,\xi]`$, $`\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{20})`$ from `MersenneTwister`$`(s)`$; $`\lVert p_0-p^\star\rVert\in[1.50,1.84]`$ over the 8 seeds (0.1 is R001’s scale; the repository uses 0.01 — see <a href="#fig:28" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:28">Figure 28</a>).

</div>

**Read this:** arms are compared at *equal* budgets (same iterations, same schedule, same seeds) except where the figure says otherwise: the schedule experiment (<a href="#fig:21" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:21">Figure 21</a>) deliberately changes the number of stages, and the optimiser experiment (<a href="#fig:25" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:25">Figure 25</a>) reports wall time because the gradient methods do different work per iteration.

## Metrics

<div class="description">

the cost (<a href="#eq:J" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:J">[eq:J]</a>) at the returned minimiser, including the sparsity term; $`J_\kappa\ge10^3`$ flags a blow-up (*plateau*). Costs at different $`\kappa`$ are not directly comparable (different restarts).

Euclidean distance between the fitted 20-vector and the true coefficients; the identification metric. Not computed by the repository; the same definition as R001.

fractional system-recovery score in $`[0,1]`$: each of the 20 coefficients earns credit 1 if it is correctly zero ($`|p_j|<0.05`$ when $`p^\star_j=0`$) or correctly non-zero within 25 % of the true value; the score is the mean credit. *support recall* (fraction of the 7 true non-zeros found) and *false positives* (true zeros with $`|p_j|\ge0.05`$) are its components.

for two arms sharing a seed, the per-seed difference of $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert`$ at a given $`\kappa`$; reported as the mean with a 95 % percentile bootstrap CI over 2000 resamples of the *seeds* (resampling unit = optimiser seed). “Cellwise” counts report in how many seeds one arm is strictly better.

seconds on one core for one stage; only used comparatively and never in a gate.

</div>

## Symbols and frozen constants

<div class="center">

| symbol | meaning | value | where frozen |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| $`N`$ | number of samples | 101 | data recipe (mod 8) |
| $`\Delta t`$ | sample spacing | 1.0 | data recipe |
| $`S`$, $`\delta t`$ | integrator sub-steps per interval, step | 10, 0.1 | driver (<a href="#fig:27" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:27">Figure 27</a> varies $`S`$) |
| $`\kappa`$, $`K`$ | window size (data intervals), number of windows | swept, $`\lceil100/\kappa\rceil`$ | schedules above |
| $`\gamma`$, $`\alpha`$ | sparsity weight, smooth-$`\ell_1`$ sharpness | $`5\times10^{-2}`$, 500 | driver (<a href="#fig:24" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:24">Figure 24</a> varies $`\gamma`$) |
| $`\sigma_{\rm rel}`$ | relative noise per component | 0.05 | data recipe (<a href="#fig:23" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:23">Figure 23</a> varies) |
| $`\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}`$ | largest noise norm in the data | 0.159 | `fhn_data_meta.json` |
| $`L`$ | Lipschitz constant $`\sup\lVert\partial f/\partial x\rVert_2`$ along the true orbit / on the box $`[-2.5,2.5]\times[-1,2]`$ | 3.05 / 5.34 | `concept_meta` |
| $`\mu`$ | logarithmic norm $`\sup\lambda_{\max}\big((J+J^\top)/2\big)`$ along the orbit | 1.17 | idem |
| $`\tilde L`$ | $`\sup\lVert\partial f/\partial p\rVert_2`$ along the orbit (Lemma 2) | 10.56 | idem |
| $`\Delta T,\Delta T_1,\Delta T_2`$ | window length $`\kappa\Delta t`$; fine window length; $`\tau_k-\tau_k^-`$ (Prop. 1) | — | manuscript |
| blow-up threshold | $`|x|>10^3`$ or NaN | $`10^3`$ | loss |

</div>

**Read this:** $`L`$ is measured, not assumed. Along the FHN limit cycle the actual amplification of an initial-state perturbation never exceeds $`\approx8`$ (<a href="#fig:08" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:08">Figure 8</a>), so every bound that carries $`e^{L\Delta T}`$ is loose by orders of magnitude for $`\Delta T\gtrsim2`$; the bounds are qualitatively right (they order the arms correctly) but not quantitatively tight.

# Provenance and what was executed

All numerics run from the frozen snapshot `deps/` (post-fix sources) through `analysis/common.jl` and `analysis/hs_core.jl`, a corrected, allocation-light, dimension-generic re-implementation of the windowed loss that is gated against the frozen mod 8 `forward_simulation_loss_windows` (relative difference $`1.9\times10^{-13}`$ over 42 evaluations, gate G2) and against the frozen mod 8 data block ($`6\times10^{-15}`$, G3). The bug scripts additionally execute `deps/prefix/` (pre-fix sources, byte-identical to commit `44abf4a`, `origin/main` at freezing time — `git fetch` was run first). SHA-256 of both snapshots: `deps/MANIFEST.md` (G1). Julia 1.11.3 with the committed environment and no package added; figures by matplotlib from CSV/JSON; nothing in Julia plots. `Distributed` cannot open sockets in the sandbox, so the 522 sweep jobs ran as 12+8+6 independent sharded processes (`REPRODUCE.md`). Realised coverage (every axis value and cell count, computed by `analysis/make_inventory.py`) is in `planning/coverage_matrix.md`; result-file hashes in `analysis/results/results_hashes.json`; every number quoted in prose is listed with its source in `analysis/number_manifest.md`.

# Part A — Concept figures

These are the slide figures. They use the real FHN data of §<a href="#sec:defs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:defs">2</a> and a deliberately *wrong* parameter vector $`p_{\rm wrong}`$ (cubic coefficient $`-0.30`$ instead of $`-1/3`$, $`\dot w`$ time-scale multiplied by 1.15; $`\lVert p_{\rm wrong}-p^\star\rVert=0.038`$) so that the single-shooting trajectory visibly drifts while the windowed segments stay close.

**Figure 1** (`figures/fig01_problem.pdf`)

!Figure 1(figures/fig01_problem.png)

***The inverse problem.** (a) The FHN states $`v(t)`$ (blue) and $`w(t)`$ (orange) with the $`N=101`$ noisy samples (dots) at spacing $`\Delta t=1`$; the thin dashed line is the exact trajectory. (b) Phase plane with the vector field (light arrows), the true orbit and the noisy samples. (c) The unknown $`2\times10`$ coefficient matrix over the monomial library $`\{1,w,w^2,w^3,v,vw,vw^2,v^2,v^2w,v^3\}`$: only 7 of 20 entries are non-zero (values shown). The task is to recover the non-zero pattern *and* the values from the dots in (a). Data: `fhn_data.csv`, `fhn_fine.csv`, `fhn_vector_field.csv`, `fhn_library.csv`.*


**Figure 2** (`figures/fig02_single_shooting.pdf`)

!Figure 2(figures/fig02_single_shooting.png)

***Single shooting.** The model is integrated once from the first datum $`y_0`$ over the whole record with the wrong parameter $`p_{\rm wrong}`$ (vermilion); thin vertical lines are the residuals to the data. The residual (right, log scale) sits at the noise level until the model slips phase near $`t\approx18`$, then grows at an observed rate $`\approx0.45`$ per time unit (the Lipschitz bound $`L=3.05`$ is an upper bound, far above it) and saturates at the size of the attractor; the cost is $`J_{100}(p_{\rm wrong})=2.60`$ (vs $`0.0099`$ at $`p^\star`$), so a tiny parameter error produces a large, non-convex cost. Data: `concept_segments.csv` (`param=wrong`, `window_size=100`), `concept_costs.csv`.*


**Figure 3** (`figures/fig03_partition.pdf`)

!Figure 3(figures/fig03_partition.png)

***The shooting partition.** Top: the data times $`t_0,\dots,t_N`$ (ticks, spacing $`\Delta t`$) and the shooting nodes $`\tau_0<\tau_1<\dots<\tau_K`$ placed at every $`\kappa`$-th datum; the windows $`[\tau_{k-1},\tau_k]`$ of length $`\Delta T=\kappa\Delta t`$ are shaded alternately. Bottom: the coarser partition obtained by removing every other node ($`K/2`$ windows of length $`2\Delta T`$) — the elementary step of guess propagation. Schematic (no data); replaces the manuscript’s `shooting_partition.png`.*


**Figure 4** (`figures/fig04_multiple_shooting.pdf`)

!Figure 4(figures/fig04_multiple_shooting.png)

***Multiple shooting.** The same wrong parameter as <a href="#fig:02" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:02">Figure 2</a>, integrated (a) as single shooting ($`\kappa=100`$, $`J=2.60`$) and (b) restarting from the datum at every 10th sample ($`\kappa=10`$, $`J=0.0140`$); windows are shaded, node markers highlighted, residual lines drawn to the data; (c) the per-datum residual magnitude on a log scale for $`\kappa=100,10,5`$ ($`J=2.60,\,0.0140,\,0.0188`$). Restarting resets the accumulated error at every node, so the exponential amplification is paid over $`\Delta T=\kappa\Delta t`$ instead of over the whole record; with $`\kappa\le10`$ the wrong model is only $`1.4`$–$`1.8\times`$ the cost of the true one, with $`\kappa=100`$ it is $`260\times`$. The flip side, visible in (c): short windows keep even a wrong model near the noise floor, i.e. they give a smooth landscape at the price of less power to discriminate $`p`$ from $`p^\star`$ — which is why the sweep must end at single shooting. Replaces `multiple_shooting.png`. Data: `concept_segments.csv`, `concept_costs.csv`.*


**Figure 5** (`figures/fig05_node_removal.pdf`)

!Figure 5(figures/fig05_node_removal.png)

***Node removal (Proposition 1).** Zoom on $`t\in[19,41]`$ with the wrong parameter: the fine partition ($`\kappa=5`$, blue segments) and the coarse one after removing the node $`\tau_k`$ at $`t=25`$ (open marker; $`\kappa=10`$, vermilion), with $`\tau_k^-=20`$ and $`\tau_k^+=30`$; the measured gap between the fine and coarse segments at $`t=37`$ is printed. After removal the segment launched at the left neighbour $`\tau_k^-`$ must cover $`[\tau_k^-,\tau_k^+]`$; the cost changes only on the windows adjacent to the removed nodes, by at most $`2|I_R|\,C_{\max}\big(e^{L(\Delta T_1+\Delta T_2)}\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}+e^{L\Delta T_1}[\tfrac{\tilde L}{L}(e^{L\Delta T_2}-1)\lVert p - p^\star\rVert+\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}]\big)`$ with $`\Delta T_1`$ the fine window length and $`\Delta T_2=\tau_k-\tau_k^-`$. Design rule: remove few nodes at a time, prefer low-noise nodes, keep $`\Delta T_2`$ small. Replaces `comparison_shooting_nodes.png`.*


**Figure 6** (`figures/fig06_guess_propagation.pdf`)

!Figure 6(figures/fig06_guess_propagation.png)

***The guess-propagation algorithm.** One-dimensional slices $`J_\kappa(p^\star+s\,u)`$ along the same random unit direction $`u`$ (the one of the 12 directions of <a href="#fig:13" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:13">Figure 13</a> with the most local minima at $`\kappa=100`$: 1, 4, 8, 25 local minima at $`\kappa=1,5,25,100`$, circled) for $`\kappa=1,5,25,100`$ (log scale; hatched band = blow-up plateau $`J=10^3`$; star = global minimum, which is at $`s=0`$ because the slices pass through $`p^\star`$). Small windows give a smooth, nearly convex landscape; large windows add local minima and a wide plateau. The algorithm solves the $`\kappa=1`$ problem from a random start and carries each minimiser (arrow) into the next, more rugged landscape, ending with a single-shooting polish. Data: `landscape_1d_slices.csv`.*


**Figure 7** (`figures/fig07_error_growth_schematic.pdf`)

!Figure 7(figures/fig07_error_growth_schematic.png)

***Error growth, schematic.** The Lemma 1 envelope $`e^{Lt}\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}`$ for single shooting (one restart at $`t_0`$) versus the sawtooth of multiple shooting, capped at $`e^{L\Delta T}\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}`$ by the restart at every node, drawn with the report’s $`L=3.05`$ and $`\lVert\eta\rVert_{\max}=0.159`$. This is the manuscript’s one-line argument; <a href="#fig:08" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:08">Figure 8</a> shows how loose the envelope is on the actual system.*


# Part B — Numerical checks of the theory

**Figure 8** (`figures/fig08_lemma1_flow_sensitivity.pdf`)

!Figure 8(figures/fig08_lemma1_flow_sensitivity.png)

***Lemma 1 (flow sensitivity to the initial state).** Amplification $`\lVert\varphi(t;p^\star,x_1)-\varphi(t;p^\star,x_2)\rVert/\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert`$ for 24 probes ($`x_1`$ = a datum at 4 different phases of the orbit, $`x_2=x_1+10^{-3}u`$ for 6 random unit directions; blue), against $`e^{Lt}`$ with $`L=\sup_{\rm orbit}\lVert\partial f/\partial x\rVert_2=3.05`$ (vermilion), $`e^{-Lt}`$ (dotted) and $`e^{\mu t}`$ with the logarithmic norm $`\mu=1.17`$ (green dashed). (a) 10 time units, (b) zoom on the first three windows. The two-sided bound holds everywhere, but the actual amplification peaks at $`\approx8`$ near the fast jump of the relaxation oscillation and then *contracts* (the limit cycle is attracting), whereas $`e^{Lt}`$ reaches $`10^{13}`$ at $`t=10`$. Data: `lemma1_flow_sensitivity.csv`, `concept_meta.json`.*


**Figure 9** (`figures/fig09_lemma2_param_sensitivity.pdf`)

!Figure 9(figures/fig09_lemma2_param_sensitivity.png)

***Lemma 2 (flow sensitivity to the parameters).** $`\lVert\varphi(t;p_1,x_0)-\varphi(t;p_2,x_0)\rVert/\lVert p_1-p_2\rVert`$ for 24 probes ($`p_2=p^\star+10^{-3}u`$, random unit $`u\in\mathbb R^{20}`$) versus the bound $`\tfrac{\tilde L}{L}(e^{Lt}-1)`$ with $`\tilde L=\sup_{\rm orbit}\lVert\partial f/\partial p\rVert_2=10.56`$. The bound holds; the measured sensitivity saturates around $`10`$–$`10^2`$ because the orbit is attracting. Data: `lemma2_param_sensitivity.csv`.*


**Figure 10** (`figures/fig10_prop1_node_removal.pdf`)

!Figure 10(figures/fig10_prop1_node_removal.png)

***Proposition 1 (node removal changes the cost by a bounded amount).** Starting from the finest partition (every datum a node, $`K=100`$) with $`\gamma=0`$: (a) keep every $`m`$-th node so that $`|I_R|=100-\lceil100/m\rceil`$ nodes are removed ($`\Delta T_2=\Delta t`$ fixed, $`\Delta T_1=m\Delta t`$ grows), and (b) remove one contiguous block of $`b`$ nodes after node 30 ($`|I_R|=b`$, $`\Delta T_2=b\Delta t`$ grows). Shown for $`p=p^\star`$ (green), a vector $`0.02`$ away from $`p^\star`$ on 6 coefficients (blue, $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert=0.06`$) and $`p_{\rm wrong}`$ of Part A (vermilion, $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert=0.04`$ concentrated on the cubic term). $`|\hat J-J|`$ grows with both $`|I_R|`$ and $`\Delta T_2`$, and much faster for the wrong parameter, as the proposition says; the bound’s rate $`e^{L\Delta T_2}`$ (grey dashed in (b)) is far steeper than the observed growth, which saturates once the removed block spans a full fast excursion. Data: `prop1_node_removal.csv`.*


# Part C — Cost landscapes

**Figure 11** (`figures/fig11_landscape_2d_v_v3.pdf`)

!Figure 11(figures/fig11_landscape_2d_v_v3.png)

***2-D slices of $`J_\kappa`$ in the $`(v,\,v^3)`$ coefficient plane of the $`\dot v`$ equation.** All other coefficients at their true values, $`x_0=y_0`$, $`\gamma=0.05`$; star = truth $`(1,-1/3)`$; grey = blow-up plateau ($`J\ge10^3`$); colour is $`\log J`$. As $`\kappa`$ grows from 1 to 100 the basin around the truth narrows by an order of magnitude and the plateau expands: any positive cubic coefficient (above the horizontal edge) makes $`\dot v\sim cv^3`$ blow up in finite time, and at $`\kappa=100`$ even $`v`$-coefficients $`>1.6`$ do. This is the geometric reason the control arm fails at large $`\kappa`$. Data: `landscape_2d_v_v3.csv`.*


**Figure 12** (`figures/fig12_landscape_2d_w_wv.pdf`)

!Figure 12(figures/fig12_landscape_2d_w_wv.png)

***2-D slices in the ($`w`$ in $`\dot v`$, $`v`$ in $`\dot w`$) plane.** Same protocol as <a href="#fig:11" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:11">Figure 11</a>; star = truth $`(-1,0.08)`$. The $`\dot w`$ coefficient (vertical axis, true value 0.08) is a slow time-scale: at $`\kappa=1`$ the cost is almost flat along it (weakly identifiable from one-interval windows), and only long windows ($`\kappa\ge10`$) pin it down — the mechanism behind the non-monotone parameter error along the sweep (<a href="#fig:15" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:15">Figure 15</a>b). Data: `landscape_2d_w_wv.csv`.*


**Figure 13** (`figures/fig13_landscape_1d_slices.pdf`)

!Figure 13(figures/fig13_landscape_1d_slices.png)

***1-D slices along random directions and the number of local minima.** Top row: $`J_\kappa(p^\star+s\,u_d)`$ for three random unit directions $`u_d\in\mathbb R^{20}`$ (colour light to dark = $`\kappa=1,2,5,10,25,50,100`$; gaps = plateau); top right: local minima per slice (mean over 12 directions, band = min–max) rising from $`1.25`$ at $`\kappa=1`$ to $`7.9`$ at $`\kappa=100`$. Bottom: the full $`s\in[-2,2]`$ range for direction 1. Larger windows sharpen the minimum (better conditioning *at* the truth) but add spurious minima and cut the finite region down to $`|s|\lesssim0.5`$. Data: `landscape_1d_slices.csv`, `landscape_1d_minima.csv`.*


**Figure 14** (`figures/fig14_hessian_conditioning.pdf`)

!Figure 14(figures/fig14_hessian_conditioning.png)

***Curvature of the data term at $`p^\star`$ versus window size.** (a) Largest and smallest Hessian eigenvalues of the data term of $`J_\kappa`$ at $`p^\star`$ (ForwardDiff, 20 parameters) and the gradient norm: $`\lambda_{\max}`$ grows from $`36`$ ($`\kappa=1`$) to $`1.2\times10^6`$ ($`\kappa=100`$) while $`\lVert\nabla J_\kappa(p^\star)\rVert`$ grows from $`0.04`$ to $`96`$ — with noisy data the truth is not a stationary point and drifts away from the minimiser as $`\kappa`$ grows. (b) The number of negative eigenvalues: the noisy cost is indefinite at $`p^\star`$ for every $`\kappa\ge2`$ (up to 6 of 20 directions), so the manuscript’s strong-convexity assumption can only hold in a neighbourhood of the *minimiser* $`p^{(\kappa)}`$, not of $`p^\star`$ (checked there in <a href="#fig:37" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:37">Figure 37</a>). (c) Sensitivity of $`J_\kappa`$ to the free initial-condition variable $`v_0`$: a shallow parabola for every $`\kappa`$, because $`x_0`$ only enters through the first residual. Data: `hessian_at_ptrue.csv`, `landscape_x0_sensitivity.csv`.*

***Guess propagation versus no propagation, 8 seeds.** (a) Cost, (b) parameter error and (c) recovery score at the minimiser of each stage; thin lines = individual seeds, thick = median; blue circles GP, green triangles best-GP, vermilion squares control. From $`\kappa=2`$ on, GP drops to $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert\approx0.22`$–$`0.38`$ and ends single shooting at $`0.32`$ (score $`0.80`$), whereas the control climbs back to the seed distance ($`1.65`$ at $`\kappa=100`$; 25 % of its seeds end on the plateau, all others in spurious minima with $`J`$ up to $`1.5`$). One GP seed (seed 1) starts on the plateau at $`\kappa=1`$ and never moves (flat line at $`1.84`$). The parameter error is *not* monotone: it is smallest at $`\kappa=5`$ ($`0.22`$) and drifts up to $`0.32`$ while the cost keeps falling — the noise-induced bias of <a href="#fig:14" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:14">Figure 14</a>. #### Three GP seeds on the plateau at $`\kappa=1`$, one forever.

Table <a href="#tab:T1" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tab:T1">Table T1</a> shows 3 GP seeds with a blow-up minimiser at $`\kappa=1`$ but only 1 from $`\kappa=2`$ on. A random start with a positive cubic coefficient of order $`0.1`$–$`0.3`$ blows up within one time unit ($`\dot v\sim cv^3`$, $`|v|\approx2`$), so the loss is $`10^3`$ at the start; if the whole initial Nelder–Mead simplex sits on the plateau the optimiser declares convergence after 0 iterations (all vertices equal) and returns the seed. Two of the three starts have a simplex vertex off the plateau at $`\kappa=2`$ and escape; seed 1 does not, at any $`\kappa`$. This is a property of the *flat* penalty, not of guess propagation; the graded penalty (<a href="#fig:22" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:22">Figure 22</a>, <a href="#fig:28" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:28">Figure 28</a>) removes it.

***Flat versus graded blow-up penalty.** The repository returns the constant $`10^3`$ on blow-up; the graded variant adds a term that decreases with the index at which the blow-up occurred. GP with the graded penalty (purple) ends at $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert=0.27`$, score $`0.83`$, with *no* seed on the plateau at any stage (c), versus $`0.32`$ / $`0.80`$ / 12.5 % for the flat penalty (blue): seed 1 is rescued. For the control the penalty changes nothing (still $`\approx1.6`$): without propagation the failure is the landscape, not the plateau. Data: `sweeps.csv` (`exp=penalty`, `main`).*


**Figure 23** (`figures/fig23_noise.pdf`)

!Figure 23(figures/fig23_noise.png)

***Observation noise.** GP (a) and control (b) along the SHORT schedule for relative noise $`\sigma_{\rm rel}\in\{0,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2\}`$ (6 seeds each; the data-noise seed is fixed so the noise realisations are scaled versions of one another); (c) final error at $`\kappa=100`$. GP ends at $`0.22`$–$`0.36`$ for $`\sigma_{\rm rel}\le0.1`$ and fails at $`0.2`$ ($`1.88`$); the control ends at $`1.6`$–$`1.7`$ at *every* noise level including $`0`$ — restarting from the seed fails because of the landscape, not the noise. Note that the GP error does not go to zero at zero noise ($`0.23`$): the remaining error is the sparsity-term shrinkage and Nelder–Mead’s finite accuracy, not noise. Data: `sweeps.csv` (`exp=noise`).*


**Figure 24** (`figures/fig24_sparsity.pdf`)

!Figure 24(figures/fig24_sparsity.png)

***Sparsity weight $`\gamma`$.** GP along the SHORT schedule for $`\gamma\in\{0,10^{-3},10^{-2},0.05,0.2,1\}`$, 6 seeds: (a) $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert`$, (b) false non-zeros, (c) score; bottom: median $`|p_j|`$ at $`\kappa=100`$ per coefficient (red boxes = true support). $`\gamma=0.05`$ (the repository default) is the best of the six ($`0.22`$, score $`0.80`$); with $`\gamma\le0.01`$ the Nelder–Mead sweep wanders into dense, wrong models ($`0.81`$–$`0.89`$, 4–6 false non-zeros), and $`\gamma\ge0.2`$ over-shrinks the true coefficients ($`0.47`$, $`1.01`$). Data: `sweeps.csv`, `sweep_minimizers.csv` (`exp=sparsity`).*


**Figure 25** (`figures/fig25_optimizers.pdf`)

!Figure 25(figures/fig25_optimizers.png)

***Optimiser: derivative-free versus AD gradient.** Nelder–Mead, BFGS and L-BFGS (exact ForwardDiff gradient of the windowed loss, possible after fix F4), with (solid) and without (dashed) propagation, 8 seeds, FULL schedule: (a) median $`\lVert p - p^\star\rVert`$, (b) wall time per stage, (c) objective evaluations per stage. BFGS+GP is the best arm ($`0.21`$, score $`0.95`$) and needs $`\approx150`$ evaluations per stage instead of $`3500`$; L-BFGS reaches the same minimiser but hits the iteration cap at large $`\kappa`$ ($`100`$ s per stage). Without propagation the gradient methods stop after one evaluation whenever the start is on the plateau (zero gradient) — 62–71 % of their stages — and otherwise converge to spurious minima. Data: `sweeps.csv` (`exp=optimizer`, `main`).*


**Figure 26** (`figures/fig26_basin.pdf`)

!Figure 26(figures/fig26_basin.png)

***Basin of attraction of a single window size.** One Nelder–Mead run (2500 iterations) of $`J_\kappa`$ from $`p_0=p^\star+r\,u`$ (10 random unit directions per radius $`r\in\{0.05,\dots,0.8\}`$) for $`\kappa=1,5,100`$: (a) fraction of starts ending within $`0.3`$ of $`p^\star`$, (b) final error (dots) and median. Single shooting ($`\kappa=100`$) only converges from $`r\le0.1`$; $`\kappa=5`$ from $`r\le0.2`$; $`\kappa=1`$ never gets below $`\approx0.15`$ (its noise/shrinkage floor) but improves every start up to $`r=0.4`$. This is the quantitative version of <a href="#fig:06" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:06">Figure 6</a>: small windows have the wide basin, large windows have the accurate minimum. Data: `sweeps.csv` (`exp=basin`).*

***Iteration budget and integrator resolution.** (a) GP with 250–5000 Nelder–Mead iterations per stage (4 seeds, SHORT): final medians $`1.72,1.43,0.61,0.27,0.20`$ — fewer than 2500 iterations in 22 dimensions is not converged; (b) sub-steps $`S\in\{1,2,5,10,20\}`$ per data interval ($`\delta t=1/S`$): $`S\ge5`$ gives the same answer ($`0.27`$–$`0.29`$), $`S=1`$ ($`\delta t=\Delta t`$) biases the fit ($`0.50`$) but never blows up; (c) wall time scales linearly with $`S`$. # Part G — Defects found and fixed

Each defect is quantified by executing the frozen pre-fix source (`deps/prefix/`) against the frozen post-fix source (`deps/`), never by re-typing; `analysis/06_bugs.jl`. Table <a href="#tab:T4" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tab:T4">Table T4</a> summarises. The fixes are in the live tree in the same commit as this report (every changed line carries the comment `R002 fix`):

- **F1** (R001; `mod 6`, `odefun_new`): the continuation lines beginning with `+` were separate, discarded statements, so the Jacobian behind the stability/eigenvalue movies was that of the *linear truncation* of the vector field. Fixed by parenthesising the RHS. All movies under `figs/window_size_plots/stability/` are wrong and should be regenerated.

- **F2** (R001; `mod 7` stiff branch of `forward_simulation_loss_windows`): the same parsing trap dropped the entire $`w`$-residual. Fixed by parenthesising. (Mod 8 already used a matrix norm and was not affected.)

- **F4** (R001; `mod 7` and `mod 8` drivers): `grad_fs_loss_window!` differentiated the single-shooting loss `fs_loss`, not `fs_loss_window`. Fixed; this is what makes the BFGS arms of <a href="#fig:25" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:25">Figure 25</a> possible.

- **F5** (R001; `plotting_window_size.jl`, `animate_contourplots!`): stale call signature (missing `unstable_param` slot, keyword `silent` instead of `silent_`). Fixed to the mod 6+ signature; *not executed here* (Makie cannot load in the sandbox), so this fix is a reading, not a measurement.

- **F6** (R001; `mod 8` driver): the `@threads` loop wrote the shared `x0`, `results_inner` and a `Dict`. Fixed with per-run copies and a lock; not a figure.

- **N1 (new)** `mod 8` driver: the sweep called the pre-refactor `odefun` (order $`1,v,w,\dots`$) while the data, `fhn_p` and the polish used the library order; the bar-chart labels `trmstr` encoded the old order and `plotSolution!` was called with an undefined name `trm`. The truth vector read in the wrong order is $`2.50`$ away from itself (<a href="#fig:34" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:34">Figure 34</a>a) and its cost at $`\kappa=1`$ is $`0.68`$ instead of $`0.018`$: the committed sweep could not have recovered the model. Fixed (sweep and plots use `odefun_generic`; labels generated from `multiindex_mapping`).

- **N2 (new)** `mod 8`, `forward_simulation_loss` (explicit branch, used by the final BFGS polish): read the *global* `data` instead of its `data_` argument, so the function ignored the data it was given (<a href="#fig:34" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:34">Figure 34</a>b). Fixed. This is the shadowing R001 asked to check when the refactor landed.

- **N3 (new, behavioural)** the committed driver had guess propagation *disabled* (`copyto!(x0, x0_)` after every stage). Replaced by an explicit `guess_mode` switch (`:propagate` default, `:best`, `:reset`).

- Minor: undefined `y0` default in `custom_integrator`; wrong bound in the window-size warning.

R001’s bug-presence gates G3, G4, G5 and G7 are retired by this report: R002’s gates G5–G9 assert the defects are present in `deps/prefix/` and absent in `deps/`.

| finding | measure | value |

| F2 (R001): mod 7 stiff branch drops the w-residual | share of J(p*) missing, κ=1/10/25/100 | 11.5 % / 9.3 % / 17.0 % / 11.2 % / 11.9 % |
| F1 (R001): mod 6 odefun_new = linear truncation | ∂v̇/∂v at u=(1.5,0.4): pre-fix vs fixed | 1 vs -1.25 |
| F4 (R001): sweep gradient = single-shooting gradient | cos∠(gκ, g100) at κ=1 / 5 | 0.180 / 0.989 |
| NEW: mod 8 driver mixed monomial orders | spurious ‖p−p*‖ between orderings | 2.501 |
| NEW: mod 8 forward_simulation_loss ignores data_ | J identical for 3 datasets pre-fix / differs post-fix | True / True |

**Figure 37** (`figures/fig37_post_hessian_path.pdf`)

!Figure 37(figures/fig37_post_hessian_path.png)

***The theory’s premises checked where they are assumed.** (a) Smallest eigenvalue of the data-term Hessian at the GP minimiser $`p^{(\kappa)}`$ returned by Nelder–Mead at every stage, 7 seeds (the plateau seed excluded; symlog scale; blue = all 20 eigenvalues positive, vermilion = at least one negative). Where the manuscript assumes local strong convexity — at the minimiser, not at $`p^\star`$ — the returned point is positive definite in only 36 % of the (seed, $`\kappa`$) cells, with on average $`0.8`$ of 20 eigenvalues slightly negative elsewhere ($`|\lambda_{\min}|\lesssim10^{-3}`$ against $`\lambda_{\max}`$ of $`10`$–$`10^6`$): Nelder–Mead stops short of a true stationary point in 22 dimensions (cf. <a href="#fig:27" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:27">Figure 27</a>a), so the premise is *not* verified at the returned iterates; the BFGS iterates of <a href="#fig:25" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:25">Figure 25</a> would be the right place to test it. (b) The cost of the *next* stage along the straight segment from $`p^{(\kappa_i)}`$ to $`p^{(\kappa_{i+1})}`$ (seed 2), relative to its value at the carried guess: it decreases monotonically along every segment, i.e. the carried guess lies inside the basin of the next minimiser — the mechanism the node-removal theorem describes. (c) Cross-evaluation (seed 2): the minimiser of $`\kappa_i`$ evaluated at every other $`\kappa_j`$ (log colour); the near-diagonal structure shows that a minimiser is good only for nearby window sizes, which is why the schedule must be gradual (<a href="#fig:21" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:21">Figure 21</a>). Data: `post_hessian_at_minimizers.csv`, `post_path_between_minimizers.csv`, `post_cross_evaluation.csv`.*

# Limitations and honest notes

- **Seeds.** 8 optimiser seeds (6 for noise/sparsity, 4 for iterations/sub-steps/Lorenz, 10 starts per radius for the basin experiment) is enough for paired CIs that exclude zero, not for tail statistics; one seed in eight starts on the plateau and is kept in every median.

- **Nelder–Mead budget.** At 2500 iterations the sweep is converged for FHN (<a href="#fig:27" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:27">Figure 27</a>a) but not for Lorenz (<a href="#fig:36" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:36">Figure 36</a>); the BFGS arms are the recommendation, and their wall times are machine-dependent.

- **The Lipschitz bounds are loose** by orders of magnitude on this attracting system (<a href="#fig:08" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:08">Figure 8</a>–<a href="#fig:10" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:10">Figure 10</a>); the figures support the theory’s *ordering* of single vs multiple shooting, not the size of the constants.

- **Not gated:** F5 (Makie) and F6 (a race) are readings; the concept figures 3 and 7 are schematics and say so.

- **Timing columns** are wall-clock on a shared 16-core machine with up to 16 concurrent processes and are only comparative.

- **Planned vs realised.** 522 planned sweep jobs; the batch was re-sharded twice (resume logic in `04_sweeps.jl`) after two shards stalled on slow L-BFGS jobs; duplicates from deterministic re-runs are removed at merge time (identical results, different wall time). The first-batch sparsity jobs (arm name without $`\gamma`$) were superseded by $`\gamma`$-named arms and are dropped at merge.

# Reproduction

See `REPRODUCE.md` for the pinned environment and the ordered commands (Julia stages 00–09, then the Python inventory, tables, figures, animation, gates, number manifest, and `pdflatex` twice). `report.md` is a full-content Markdown rendition of this document generated from the same sources.
